# ChunkLand — bundled reference

> Single-file bundle of ChunkLand's English reference material, for language models that would rather read one document than follow links. The per-page documents under `docs/en/` are canonical; if this file and a page disagree, the page is right.
>
> Source version in this checkout: **0.1.0**. No release has been published. Supported runtime: **Folia 26.2** on **Java 25**, with **AceLib 1.3.0** required. Paper is not supported. The `api-version: '26.1.2'` in `plugin.yml` and the paper-api 26.1.2 compile dependency are build markers, not a compatibility claim.

## What the plugin is

A land-claim plugin for Folia. Players fence off a claim with a selection wand, and from then on each attempt to break, place, open, use, fight inside, or enter that claim is decided individually at the moment it happens. Claims are chunk-aligned rectangles. Claims can grow, shrink, be released, renamed and deleted; paid chunks are refunded.

## Obtaining and installing

No published artifact, no Maven coordinate, no JitPack entry. Build from a checkout:

```bash
./scripts/build-acelib.sh          # AceLib 1.3.0 into $XDG_CACHE_HOME/chunkland-acelib, SHA-256 verified
./gradlew build --no-daemon --console=plain
```

Output: `chunkland-plugin/build/libs/chunkland-plugin-0.1.0.jar` — self-contained, with `chunkland-api`, SQLite and SnakeYAML embedded. `chunkland-api/build/libs/chunkland-api-0.1.0.jar` is produced alongside. Copy the plugin jar into `plugins/`. AceLib must already be in `plugins/` because `plugin.yml` declares `depend: [AceLib]`.

First start creates `plugins/ChunkLand/` with `config.yml`, `config-last-known-good.yml`, `lang/en_US.yml`, `lang/zh_TW.yml` and `chunkland.db` (SQLite — all land, chunk, permission and ledger data). Language files are written only when missing and never overwritten, so keys added by a later version come from the jar while your existing values stay.

**There is no reload command.** Edit `config.yml`, restart. Bukkit `/reload` is not supported either.

Optional plugins: a Vault-ecosystem economy plugin for claim pricing, LuckPerms for quota metadata, CoreProtect for `/land history`. None are required; the plugin starts without them and the corresponding features report unavailable.

## The three things that surprise people

**Entry is allowed by default.** `subject-defaults.global.ENTRY: ALLOW` means an unbanned stranger can walk into a loaded claim. Entry bans still deny, because a ban is decided at the land binding layer with deny priority. Set `ENTRY: DENY` to close claims to everyone who is not trusted.

**The eleven land rules cannot be changed.** PVP, terrain explosion, entity explosion, fire spread, fire burn, mob griefing, fluid flow, pistons, hopper transfer, hostile mob spawning and passive mob spawning run on built-in defaults. Inside a land, fluid flow, pistons, hopper transfer and both kinds of mob spawning follow vanilla; PVP, explosions, fire spread and burn, and mob griefing are denied. A piston, fluid or hopper that reaches across a land boundary — in either direction — is always refused. The `rule-defaults` block in `config.yml` is a commented example that is not wired to anything.

**All 29 permission nodes default to `op`.** A regular player cannot claim land, trust a member or open the management screen until an operator grants the node explicitly.

## Commands

`/land` and `/chunkland`. "Player" means the command is refused from the console.

### Land actions

| Subcommand | Usage | Permission |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `help` | `/land help [subcommand]` | `chunkland.command.land.help` |
| `wand` | `/land wand` | `chunkland.command.land.wand` |
| `claim` | `/land claim <land_name>` | `chunkland.command.land.claim` |
| `confirm` | `/land confirm <generation> <revision> <land_name>` | `chunkland.command.land.confirm` |
| `expand` | `/land expand` | `chunkland.command.land.expand` |
| `shrink` | `/land shrink` | `chunkland.command.land.shrink` |
| `unclaim` | `/land unclaim` | `chunkland.command.land.shrink` |
| `rename` | `/land rename <new_name>` | `chunkland.command.land.rename` |
| `delete` | `/land delete confirm <revision>` | `chunkland.command.land.delete` |
| `subland` | `/land subland (select\|create\|update\|delete\|extend) [generation revision] [name]` | `chunkland.command.land.subland` |

`claim` alone proposes; `confirm` commits. `shrink` and `unclaim` share one node.

### Permissions on a land

| Subcommand | Usage | Permission |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `trust` | `/land trust <player>` | `chunkland.command.land.trust` |
| `untrust` | `/land untrust <player>` | `chunkland.command.land.untrust` |
| `ban` | `/land ban <player>` | `chunkland.command.land.ban` |
| `unban` | `/land unban <player>` | `chunkland.command.land.unban` |
| `default` | `/land default <action> [ALLOW\|DENY\|INHERIT]` | `chunkland.command.land.default` |
| `binding` | `/land binding (bind\|unbind) player <player> <profile>` | `chunkland.command.land.binding` |
| `binding` | `/land binding (bind\|unbind) group <group> <profile> [--in-subland]` | `chunkland.command.land.binding` |

### Groups, profiles, queries, administration

| Subcommand | Usage | Permission |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `group` | `/land group create <group>` | `chunkland.command.land.group` |
| `group` | `/land group list` | `chunkland.command.land.group` |
| `group` | `/land group add <group> <player>` | `chunkland.command.land.group` |
| `group` | `/land group remove <group> <player>` | `chunkland.command.land.group` |
| `group` | `/land group delete <group>` | `chunkland.command.land.group` |
| `profile` | `/land profile create <profile>` | `chunkland.command.land.profile` |
| `profile` | `/land profile list` | `chunkland.command.land.profile` |
| `profile` | `/land profile set <profile> <action> <state>` | `chunkland.command.land.profile` |
| `profile` | `/land profile delete <profile>` | `chunkland.command.land.profile` |
| `explain` | `/land explain <action>` | `chunkland.command.land.explain` |
| `inspect` | `/land inspect [player]` | `chunkland.command.land.inspect` |
| `log` | `/land log [u:<player-uuid>] [t:<duration>] [a:<action>] [land:<land-uuid>] [world:<world-uuid>] [limit:<n>] [page:<n>]` | `chunkland.command.land.log` |
| `history` | `/land history` | `chunkland.command.land.history` |
| `manage` | `/land manage` | `chunkland.command.land.manage` |
| `bypass` | `/land bypass [on\|off]` | `chunkland.admin.bypass` |
| `admin` | `/land admin ledger list [state]` / `show [operation]` / `resolve <operation> [RESOLVED\|REFUNDED\|IGNORED]` | `chunkland.admin.ledger` |
| `admin` | `/land admin orphan list` | `chunkland.admin.orphan` |
| `admin` | `/land admin orphan purge <world-uuid> confirm <nonce>` | `chunkland.admin.orphan` |

`explain`, `inspect` and `manage` require standing inside a land you manage. `<action>` matches `ProtectionActionType` names case-insensitively and must be exact; tab completion offers valid names by prefix. `orphan purge` is irreversible and does not refund.

### Diagnostics

| Subcommand | Usage | Permission |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `m0message` | `/chunkland m0message [locale]` | `chunkland.debug.m0message` |
| `m0test` | `/chunkland m0test [scheduler\|gui\|form\|cancelall]` | `chunkland.debug.m0test` |
| `viz` | `/chunkland viz <start\|stop\|status>` | `chunkland.debug.visualization` |

### Player reference resolution

Raw UUID text first. Then an exact, case-sensitive online name. Then an offline-player lookup on an async executor, which may block on a profile request and fails closed on timeout. It only answers for players the server already knows — has played before, or is online. Everything else reports an unknown target. There is no partial-name matching.

## Permissions

29 nodes, all `default: op`. Enforcement is on the subcommand, not on the land; who a player may actually trust is decided separately by the land's own permission layers.

22 land nodes: `help`, `wand`, `claim`, `confirm`, `trust`, `untrust`, `default`, `ban`, `unban`, `binding`, `group`, `profile`, `subland`, `expand`, `shrink`, `rename`, `delete`, `explain`, `inspect`, `log`, `history`, `manage` — all under `chunkland.command.land.`.

4 admin nodes: `chunkland.admin.bypass` (separate by design — holding it never grants ledger, orphan or steward powers, and holding those never grants bypass), `chunkland.admin.ledger`, `chunkland.admin.orphan`, `chunkland.admin.serverland` (stewardship over the server's own land; not bound to a `/land` subcommand).

3 debug nodes: `chunkland.debug.m0message`, `chunkland.debug.m0test`, `chunkland.debug.visualization`.

## Configuration

Every accepted top-level key is validated on load. An unrecognised top-level key fails the load loudly rather than being ignored.

### messages

| Key | Default |
| --- | --- |
| `messages.default-locale` | `en_US` (bundled: `en_US`, `zh_TW`) |
| `messages.cooldown-seconds` | `2` |

### audit

| Key | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `audit.retention-days` | `180` | `0` keeps forever and runs no purge. Otherwise deletes audit rows strictly older than the cutoff, in batches on the persistence thread. Land, chunk and ledger rows are never touched |

### economy

| Key | Default |
| --- | --- |
| `economy.enabled` | `false` — purchases off: claims and expands are free and need no economy plugin |
| `economy.currency.code` | `EMC` |
| `economy.currency.scale` | `2` (100 minor = 1 major) |

Default tiers, priced per chunk by the owner's total chunk count across all Player Lands (never Server Land), where each `until` is exclusive on the previous bound `(previousUntil, until]`:

| Range | Price per chunk |
| --- | --- |
| first 20 | `1.00` |
| 20–50 | `2.00` |
| 50–100 | `4.00` |
| beyond 100 (`unbounded`) | `8.00` |

The table must stay a contiguous partition ending in `unbounded`; a gap, overlap, negative, non-finite or overflowing entry fails the load and keeps the previous snapshot, so player claims fail closed instead of being repriced. Refunds always come from the durable per-chunk cost basis, never from the tiers, so editing tiers never changes a past refund. Do not change `currency.scale` while the ledger holds rows.

With `economy.enabled: false` (the default, and also the behaviour of a file with no `economy` section) nothing is charged and `limits` alone bounds a player; free chunks refund nothing. With `economy.enabled: true` a Vault-ecosystem economy plugin is required and a player claim without one is refused. Chunks bought while enabled still refund their recorded price after the switch is turned off.

### limits

| Key | Default |
| --- | --- |
| `limits.max-lands-per-player` | `5` |
| `limits.max-total-chunks-per-player` | `10` |
| `limits.max-chunks-per-land` | `10` |
| `limits.max-sublands-per-land` | `16` |
| `limits.max-selection-side-length` | `32` |
| `limits.max-selection-chunks` | `1024` |
| `limits.max-decision-cache-entries` | `4096` (`0` disables reuse; every decision recomputes, still fail-closed) |

`/land inspect` reports which limit applied and which layer it came from — this file, LuckPerms metadata, or the built-in default.

### selection

| Key | Default | Range |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `selection.session-timeout-seconds` | `600` | — |
| `selection.visualization-max-segments` | `256` | 1–4096 |
| `selection.visualization-max-particles-per-tick` | `512` | 1–1024 |
| `selection.visualization-render-distance-blocks` | `64` | 8–128 |
| `selection.visualization-refresh-interval-ticks` | `10` | 1–200 |

Player-scoped, never queries terrain.

### feedback

Shown to the denied player only; changes nothing about what is allowed.

| Key | Default | Range |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `feedback.entry-wall-enabled` | `true` | — |
| `feedback.entry-wall-radius-blocks` | `6` | 2–16 |
| `feedback.entry-wall-particle-size-percent` | `160` | 25–400 (100 = vanilla) |
| `feedback.entry-wall-points-per-block` | `2` | 1–4 |
| `feedback.entry-wall-cooldown-millis` | `2000` | 100–60000 |
| `feedback.action-mark-enabled` | `true` | — |
| `feedback.action-mark-particle-size-percent` | `110` | 25–400 |
| `feedback.action-mark-cooldown-millis` | `400` | 100–60000 |
| `feedback.push-out-distance-blocks` | `3` | 1–8 |
| `feedback.push-out-cooldown-millis` | `500` | 100–60000 |

Keep the push-out cooldown at or below the time a player needs to walk the distance back — about 500 ms for 3 blocks — or the player is held on cancelled moves and the screen stutters.

Landing spots only use already-loaded chunks from the current region; the plugin never loads a chunk to find one. With no safe spot it falls back to the pre-entry position, then to cancelling the move.

### worlds

| Key | Default |
| --- | --- |
| `worlds.<name>.claim-enabled` | `true` for unlisted worlds |
| `worlds.<name>.vertical-mode` | `PER_CHUNK_DEPTH` or `FULL_HEIGHT` |

Shipped: `world` claim-enabled; `world_nether` and `world_the_end` disabled. Switching `vertical-mode` changes how effective depth is read and never migrates or rewrites stored depths. World names are case-sensitive; unknown worlds warn and are ignored.

### subject-defaults

Answers "may this actor act?" per `ProtectionActionType`. Separate from `rule-defaults`, which answers "can this mechanic happen here?" per `LandRuleType`; the two never fall back to each other.

Shape: `subject-defaults.global.<ACTION>` and `subject-defaults.worlds.<world>.<ACTION>`, values `ALLOW` / `DENY` / `INHERIT`. A missing section, a missing entry or an explicit `INHERIT` all mean fall through to the next resolver layer, ending at implicit `DENY`. Action keys are case-insensitive. Land bindings, land defaults and subland layers are not configured here — no durable source is wired, so they stay `INHERIT`.

### rule-defaults

Documented in the shipped file as a commented example. **Not wired to anything.** Editing it has no effect.

## Configuration sources and recovery

- **File present but unreadable, unparseable or invalid** → falls back to the last-known-good copy; with no usable copy, to a deliberately conservative configuration. This path never substitutes the built-in defaults, and protection is never silently widened.
- **File missing, fresh install** (no trace of previous use) → generates `config.yml` from built-in defaults and starts on it. Once.
- **File missing after previous use** → no default file generated; last-known-good copy, or the conservative configuration.

The conservative configuration can be **stricter**: new claims disabled in every world, economy operations disabled so pricing is unavailable, protection coverage tightened with deny as the default. Deliberate — a corrupt or missing file must not quietly relax protection.

Console output: `INFO` with the generated file's absolute path and the restart requirement on a fresh install; `ERROR` with the config path, the fallback used, the failing key path (e.g. `worlds.world.vertical-mode`) and that built-in defaults were not used, on corruption or on a missing-after-use file; `WARNING` if the default file cannot be written, in which case the plugin still starts on the in-memory built-in defaults.

Recovery: stop the server, fix `plugins/ChunkLand/config.yml` or restore the missing settings, start the server. The original file is never overwritten, deleted or renamed on failure.

> This behaviour is confirmed at the code and automated-test level. It has not been re-verified on a live server: generating the file, console wording, and the full repair-restart-apply cycle have not been run.

## API

There is no published artifact, no Maven coordinate, and **no `ServicesManager` registration**. Depend on the locally built jar with `compileOnly` and declare `depend: [ChunkLand]`.

```java
ChunkLandPlugin plugin = (ChunkLandPlugin) Bukkit.getPluginManager().getPlugin("ChunkLand");
ChunkLandApi api = plugin.getReadApi();           // never null; empty view before enable and after disable
ChunkLandEventBus bus = plugin.publicEventBus();  // null only before the first enable
```

| Accessor | Nullability | Lifetime |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `getReadApi()` | Never null | Safe to cache; reads the live snapshot each call, so later changes are visible. A cached handle keeps returning empty after disable rather than reviving on the next enable |
| `publicEventBus()` | `null` only before the first enable. A disable leaves the previous bus in place, so a stale handle is non-null but permanently silent | Acquire it per enable. Re-acquire after every enable and never keep a handle across a disable |

### ChunkLandApi

```java
Optional<LandSnapshot> getLandSnapshot(LandId landId);
Optional<SubLandSnapshot> getSubLandSnapshot(SubLandId subLandId);
Optional<OwnerRef> getOwner(LandId landId);
boolean can(UUID actor, LandId landId, ProtectionActionType action);
Optional<PermissionState> getRule(LandId landId, LandRuleType rule);
Optional<Integer> getProtectionDepth(LandId landId);
```

| Method | Wired | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `getLandSnapshot` | Yes | Empty for unknown id |
| `getSubLandSnapshot` | Yes | Searches the snapshot's subland indexes |
| `getOwner` | Yes | Derived from the land snapshot |
| `getProtectionDepth` | Yes | `PER_CHUNK_DEPTH` lands report their stored minimum depth; `FULL_HEIGHT` lands report the world minimum. Reads never rewrite stored depths |
| `can` | **No** | Always `false` |
| `getRule` | **No** | Always `Optional.empty()` |

`can` and `getRule` are not backed by production data: `getReadApi()` injects a permission-context provider returning `null` and a rule lookup returning `Optional.empty()`. `can()` maps a `null` context to `false`; `getRule()` has nothing to report. Both are fail-closed answers working as designed. Do not build features on them — for diagnosis, have a player in the land run `/land explain <action>`.

Contract for all six: callable from any thread; one volatile snapshot per call; no I/O; never loads a chunk; returns only immutable values. Unknown ids return empty; a null argument throws `NullPointerException`.

### Events

```java
<E> void register(Class<E> eventType, ChunkLandEventListener<? super E> listener);
<E> void unregister(Class<E> eventType, ChunkLandEventListener<? super E> listener);
<E> void publish(E event);   // called by ChunkLand
```

Dispatch is synchronous on the publishing thread. Pre events run before any economy or durable side effect; a throwing Pre listener cancels the mutation, which then produces zero side effects. Post events run after the durable commit and the runtime snapshot publish; a throwing Post listener is caught, logged and isolated, and the committed mutation stands.

Listeners must return immediately: no blocking, no I/O, no waiting, no Bukkit world access outside the matching Folia thread. Post listeners run on the async continuation after the commit. `NoopChunkLandEventBus.instance()` is the inert implementation for tests.

There are 16 event types in `com.smile.chunkland.api.event`: `LandCreatePreEvent`, `LandCreatePostEvent`, `LandDeletePreEvent`, `LandDeletePostEvent`, `LandChunkAddPreEvent`, `LandChunkAddPostEvent`, `LandChunkRemovePreEvent`, `LandChunkRemovePostEvent`, `SubLandPreEvent`, `SubLandPostEvent`, `LandEnterEvent`, `LandLeaveEvent`, `SubLandEnterEvent`, `SubLandLeaveEvent`, `PermissionChangedEvent`, `RuleChangedEvent`. The five `*PreEvent` types are cancellable. **`RuleChangedEvent` is declared and wired on both channels but never fired** — land rules have no writable interface, so nothing constructs it and a listener for it never runs.

Each public event also has a Bukkit view class under `com.smile.chunkland.event.bukkit`, named after the event with the suffix changed: `LandCreatePostEvent` → `LandCreatePostBukkitEvent`, `PermissionChangedEvent` → `PermissionChangedBukkitEvent`. All extend `ChunkLandBukkitEvent`. The views exist for plugins that cannot take a compile-time dependency; `RuleChangedBukkitEvent` is subject to the same never-fired caveat.

### Domain types

`api.land`: `LandId`, `SubLandId`, `LandSnapshot`, `SubLandSnapshot`, `OwnerRef`, `LandName`, `LandNameKey`, `ChunkKey`, `Cuboid`, `SubLandTopologyValidator`, `LandNameUniqueness`.
`api.permission`: `ProtectionActionType`, `Permission`, `PermissionState`, `PermissionDecision`, `PermissionResolver`, `PermissionContext`, `PermissionSubject`, `PermissionBinding`, `DecisionSource`, `SubjectPermissionTier`.
`api.rule`: `LandRuleType`, `LandRule`.
`api.geometry`: `ChunkGeometry`, `BoundaryExtractor`, `BoundarySegment`, `Direction`.
`api.money`: `Money`, `Currency`, `PricingTable`, `PricingTier`, `CostBasisCalculator`, `CostBasisAllocation`, `ChunkCoordinate`.
`api.limit`: `LimitType`, `LimitResult`, `LimitSource`, `ExternalLimitProvider`.
`api.mutation`: `ChunkLandMutations`, `MutationRequest`, `MutationKind`, `MutationResult`, `MutationOutcome`.
`api.history`: `HistoryQuery`, `HistoryResult`, `HistoryEntry`, `WorldHistoryProvider`.

`ProtectionActionType` has 40 constants, each declaring the `DecisionSource` it resolves from.

`SUBJECT_PERMISSION` (22): `BLOCK_BREAK`, `BLOCK_PLACE`, `CONTAINER_OPEN`, `WORKSTATION_USE`, `DOOR_USE`, `BUTTON_USE`, `LEVER_USE`, `REDSTONE_USE`, `BUCKET_USE`, `ENTRY`, `VEHICLE_USE`, `ENTITY_INTERACT`, `ENTITY_DAMAGE`, `ITEM_FRAME`, `ARMOR_STAND`, `HANGING_ENTITY`, `FARMLAND_TRAMPLE`, plus `MANAGE_MEMBER`, `MANAGE_PERMISSION`, `MANAGE_SUBLAND`, `EXPAND_LAND`, `DELETE_LAND` — where the owner guarantee applies and the owner always passes without admin bypass.

`LAND_RULE` (18): `PLAYER_DAMAGE_PLAYER`, `PISTON_MOVE`, `FLUID_FLOW`, `HOPPER_TRANSFER`, `FIRE_SPREAD`, `FIRE_BURN`, `EXPLOSION_TERRAIN`, `EXPLOSION_ENTITY`, `MOB_GRIEFING`, `HOSTILE_MOB_SPAWN`, `PASSIVE_MOB_SPAWN`, `BLOCK_MOVE_IN`, `BLOCK_MOVE_OUT`, `FLUID_ENTER`, `FLUID_EXIT`, `ITEM_TRANSFER_IN`, `ITEM_TRANSFER_OUT`, `DISPENSER_CROSS_BOUNDARY`.

`LandRuleType` has 11 values: `PVP`, `EXPLOSION_TERRAIN`, `EXPLOSION_ENTITY`, `FIRE_SPREAD`, `FIRE_BURN`, `MOB_GRIEFING`, `FLUID_FLOW`, `PISTON`, `HOPPER_TRANSFER`, `HOSTILE_MOB_SPAWN`, `PASSIVE_MOB_SPAWN`.

`chunkland-api` is pure domain. A build guard fails the build if it declares any external production dependency — no Bukkit, no SQL, no AceLib.

## Known limitations

Ignition is unprotected — fire spread and burn are blocked, but nothing checks the act of starting a fire, so lava can light one and it must be put out by hand.

Land rules cannot be changed from any interface.

`/land manage` works, and its only remaining limit is that adding from a roster page offers online players only; use `/land trust` or `/land unban` for offline players. Bedrock players get the same operations as forms, and a step with no form yet tells the player to use chat.

Refusal messages on the action bar render in the server's default locale, not per player.

Selection is rectangle-only — per-chunk add and remove is not implemented, and both wand buttons do the same thing. After a subland depth `extend`, run the create or update confirmation once more; the live index refreshes on the next confirmation.

A banned player already inside is not removed immediately — they are pushed out on their next movement, to the nearest verified exit about 3 blocks past the boundary, or the world spawn if no exit exists. Push-out cooldown defaults to 500 ms.

Entry is judged from a movement's start and end points only. A subland thinner than one tick of travel, with start and end both outside it, can be crossed and is not judged. Elytra, ice boats, a trident, a long fall or plugin movement can do this. Damage, placing, containers, interaction and combat after the crossing are still judged per action at the actual position, so crossing grants nothing; land-level bans are whole-chunk and cannot be crossed; walking, sprinting and jumping move under one block per tick. Workaround: make a boundary subland 4+ blocks thick vertically and 8+ horizontally — reasoned, not measured — or use a land-level ban or the ENTRY default. Confirmed from code and static analysis, not reproduced at speed on a live server.

`/tp` into a claim is not intercepted. An operator teleporting a player in is not blocked by entry rules; the player can then move and walk out, and was not pushed out during testing. Walking entry is still blocked. There is no setting or command that brings `/tp` under entry control — use `/land ban` and control administrative permission. Verified on Folia 26.2 with walking blocked and `/tp` not blocked in the same session; it comes from how the server teleports, not from a setting. Only `/tp` was checked.

Atomic authorisation compares the authorisation generation inside the transaction and covers database-backed writes only — trust and untrust, bindings, groups and members, permission profiles, and land defaults. A rename does not advance the generation. In-memory sources (config defaults, admin bypass, server-land steward) take no part in the in-transaction comparison; their revocation is visible only at the gate before a write is submitted, so an in-flight write can still succeed after such a revocation. There is no fixed upper bound on the wait — writes share one persistence thread and queue. Database revocations are always caught.

Behaviour not listed here is not promised by this document.

## Repository layout for contributors

| Path | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `chunkland-api` | Domain types, `ChunkLandApi`, event bus interface. Pure domain, build-guarded |
| `chunkland-plugin` | The server plugin: protection, persistence, commands, GUI and forms, economy, config |
| `docs/en`, `docs/zh-TW`, `docs/zh-CN` | Three-language documentation, identical file names |
| `LIMITATIONS.md` | Traditional Chinese delivery copy of the limitations |
| `scripts/build-acelib.sh` | Downloads and verifies AceLib 1.3.0 into the local cache |

Build and test: `./gradlew build --no-daemon --console=plain` runs `check` as well as the tests. Archives drop file timestamps and fix entry order, so two clean builds of the same source produce byte-identical jars.

Protection is fail-closed: the registry starts empty and only becomes readable for occupancy after the startup rebuild publishes a complete snapshot. Until then an empty result means unknown, not wilderness, and the answer is deny. Decision cache hits are scoped to one policy epoch.
